newsitem.title: THAILAND: FORECAST-Thai data seen showing economy slowing.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Thai data seen showing economy slowing.

text.p: Key monthly economic indicators due for release by the Bank of Thailand on Thursday will probably show a sustained slowing of the Thai economy, market analysts said on Tuesday.

They said August trade and current account deficits were expected to narrow marginally from those in recent months as imports fell on weak domestic demand and exports registered small year-on-year growth after a 1.2 percent decline in July.

"We would probably see August exports rising at the most three to four percent year-on-year and continued slowdown in bank credit growth and private investment," said Chatchai Saelee of Chao Phaya Finance and Securities Co.
Chatchai forecast that sluggish exports, the main factor for Thailand's slowest economic growth in a decade this year, would rise five to six percent for the whole 1996 against 23.6 percent in 1995.
Deputy prime minister Amnuay Viravan said on Monday exports rose 3.1 percent during January/August and he expected exports growth of five percent to be posted for all of 1996.
The central bank data is eagerly awaited by the financial markets as a gauge of the health of the slwoing national economy.
Parametr Suwansiri of Capital Nomura Plc said he saw a current business downturn lasting until mid-1997 although its impact would not be as severe as that of a recession.
"Bank asset quality would be a market focus in the first half of next year and local lending rates would not ease much from current levels until the second half of 1997," he said.

The chief economist of the National Economic and Social Development Board (NESDB), Thailand's official think tank, said on Tuesday he expects gross domestic product to expand at a 10-year low of 7.0-7.5 percent in 1996 against 8.6 in 1995.
Chatchai of Chao Phaya said the market would watch more closely the October inflation due for release by the commerce ministry on Friday.
He expects the October consumer price index to rise 4.8 percent year-on-year after a 4.6 percent increase in September because of flood-induced higher food cost and diesel prices in October.
The analyst said overall 1996 inflation would range 5.8-6.0 percent against 5.5 projected by the central bank in July and 5.8 in 1995.
